item.title: 2026-W32 — The 95-point gap at Hormuz
item.description:
# The 95-point gap at Hormuz
The daily IGRM composite closed 6 August at 48.9, down from 70.0 a week earlier. The trailing seven-day composite was 61.5. Those numbers answer different questions: the daily score ranks one day's coverage share against each channel's own trailing 730 days; the seven-day score averages a week of those daily ranks. A quieter close can still sit inside a loud week.

item.title: 2026-W31 — The largest movement in this week's data was also the easiest to misread. The China/Eastern Border channel rose by 59.8 percentile points, yet the underlying news flow was dominated not by military escalation but by diplomacy. Coverage centred on Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri's visit to Beijing, where both sides reaffirmed the importance of maintaining peace along the Line of Actual Control, alongside repeated reports denying fresh Chinese encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh. Even cultural events such as the Tawang pilgrimage contributed to sustained media attention. The result is a useful reminder that heightened salience should not automatically be interpreted as heightened danger.
